newsitem.title: DENMARK: Foreign buying lifts Danish bond prices.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying lifts Danish bond prices.

text.p: Foreign interest in Danish mortgage-linked paper also gave government long-bond prices a lift on Tuesday and dealers saw no immediate sign of a falloff in demand.
"The good level of interest looks like continuing," a trader said.
At 1200 GMT the new benchmark seven percent state bond due 2007 traded at 104.10, up from Monday's 103.41, in turnover of more than 1.3 billion crowns.
The outgoing benchmark eight percent 2006 bond traded at 111.49, up from 111.06, in turnover of one billion crowns.
Its June future rose 0.64 point to 111.24, with 435 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 climbed 0.85 point to 90.00.
Based on the 2007 bond, the 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed to 75 basis points from an earlier 79 bp. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
